elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 1(b): "Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards." This is framed as a covenant rather than a warranty, but the operative professional/workmanlike standard is present and unchanged.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "each software deliverable provided under a Statement of Work will conform in all material respects to its documentation and Specifications".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Insertion sets "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" for software deliverables, not twelve (12) months.
Insertion sets "a period of thirty (30) days following performance" for the Services, not ninety (90) days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Contractor shall, at Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software deliverable or Services...".
Inserted: "...or refund the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Section 5(a) warrants only that performance "to its knowledge, does not and shall not violate any applicable law" — the knowledge qualifier is retained and no unqualified compliance-with-laws warranty was added.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code, virus or disabling-device warranty appears anywhere in Section 5 or in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted express software warranty: "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each software deliverable provided under a Statement of Work will conform in all material respects to its documentation and Specifications" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at exactly the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will conform to the requirements of the applicable Statement of Work" — meets the 30-day floor with a defined conformance standard.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall, at Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software deliverable or Services".
"...or refund the fees paid for them" — refund remedy expressly available.

reasons: Finding status of deviation is correct: before the redline the Agreement contained no conformance warranty, no warranty period and no repair/replace/refund remedy, and the only law-compliance warranty is knowledge-qualified — a failure of every material fallback term, not a mere sub-element gap.

Fallback level is complete: 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, 30-day Services warranty, and both repair/replacement and refund remedies all appear in operative inserted language, not merely in the margin comment.

Preferred level is not complete (software period is 90 days not 12 months, Services period is 30 days not 90 days, the law-compliance warranty remains knowledge-qualified, and there is no malicious-code warranty). That is acceptable because the claimed target is the fallback.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion, no deletion or paraphrase of Sections 1(b), 5(a), 5(c) or the 5(e) disclaimer, and no survival tail, at-own-expense language, notice procedure or extra damages categories. Two mild expansions were tolerated as necessary drafting rather than extras — 'and Specifications' (a defined term; a consulting MSA may have no product 'documentation', so the reference makes the warranty operable) and 'at Company's election' (the checklist is silent on who elects, though the playbook model language uses Vendor's option and Vendor may push back on Customer election; concede to 'at Contractor's option' if resisted rather than lose the clause).

Intent is preserved: Section 5(e) states the express warranties are in lieu of implied warranties, so the new express warranty survives the disclaimer without amendment; no cross-reference, defined term or commercial mechanic is left dangling, and the retained non-infringement and authority warranties are unaffected.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in substance): the insertion is rendered as an unlettered paragraph after Section 5(e); designate it as Section 5(f) so future cross-references to the warranty subsections stay clean.
